name: 19068-repeatedimage-qwen25vl7b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one vLLM engine, served in-process through guidellm's vllm_python backend.
architecture: vision-language decoder (Qwen2_5_VLForConditionalGeneration, 8.29B params, ~16.6 GB bf16); the ViT keeps native resolution, so a 1920x1080 image is 2691 image tokens.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=32, warmup 30%, no cooldown, bounded at 2000 requests with a 900 s safety cap, seed static 19068.
workload: the local request file `configs/data/repeat-pool-1080p.jsonl`, 2400 rows of which the bound consumes 2000; each row is one 1920x1080 JPEG, a 13-token question and 128 output tokens (max_tokens=128, ignore_eos). Only 32 distinct images exist, `configs/data/pool/img_00.jpg` .. `img_31.jpg`, and row N uses image N mod 32. `configs/data/make-pool.py` regenerates the JPEGs and the JSONL byte-for-byte from seed 19068; the JSONL holds ABSOLUTE image paths, so it must be regenerated rather than copied when the item moves.
purpose: A visual question-answering service for full-HD screenshots, answering short questions from 32 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine is a source checkout, named by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.

model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct
tensor-parallel-size: 1
dtype: bfloat16
# A 1920x1080 prompt measures 2707 tokens plus 128 generated; 8192 clears that with room.
max-model-len: 8192
enable-prefix-caching: true
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
# `mm-processor-kwargs` is deliberately absent: the processor's own min_pixels/max_pixels are left
# alone, so a 1080p image is not clamped and the token count above holds.
